title: Average Product Rating (Minimum 5 Reviews Required)
description:
Calculate the average rating for each product, but **only include products that have at least 5 reviews**. Order results by average rating descending.

**Table: reviews** — `review_id`, `product_id`, `product_name`, `rating`

Output columns: `product_id`, `product_name`, `review_count`, `avg_rating`. Order by `avg_rating DESC`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE reviews (review_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, product_name VARCHAR, rating INTEGER); INSERT INTO reviews VALUES (1,101,'Widget A',4),(2,101,'Widget A',5),(3,101,'Widget A',3),(4,101,'Widget A',4),(5,101,'Widget A',5),(6,102,'Gadget B',5),(7,102,'Gadget B',4),(8,102,'Gadget B',3),(9,103,'Doohickey C',3),(10,103,'Doohickey C',4),(11,103,'Doohickey C',5),(12,103,'Doohickey C',2),(13,103,'Doohickey C',4);
solution_sql: SELECT product_id, product_name, COUNT(*) AS review_count, ROUND(AVG(rating::NUMERIC), 2) AS avg_rating FROM reviews GROUP BY product_id, product_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_rating DESC;

test_cases.description: Widget A has 5 reviews (avg 4.20), Gadget B has 3 reviews (excluded), Doohickey C has 5 reviews (avg 3.60)

hints: Use HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 to exclude products with fewer than 5 reviews.
Wrap AVG(rating) with ROUND(..., 2) for a clean decimal output; cast to NUMERIC first for precision.
Gadget B has only 3 reviews and will be filtered out by the HAVING clause.
explanation: Widget A: 5 reviews with ratings 4,5,3,4,5 → avg = 21/5 = 4.20 ✓. Gadget B: only 3 reviews → excluded by HAVING. Doohickey C: 5 reviews with ratings 3,4,5,2,4 → avg = 18/5 = 3.60 ✓. Only Widget A and Doohickey C pass the minimum review threshold.
